patch.scope: Two implementation files; five proposed candidate files below include test-only additions/change.

boundary_analysis.invariant: Original fallback and actual default selection
boundary_analysis.evidence: cpu.c only adds MCKERNEL_RUST_X86_CPU_HELPERS ABI forwarding to rust_x86_save_fp_regs(thread,xsave_available,xsave_size,xsave_mask), with original allocator/save bytes in #else. Complete pre-save CPU reconstructs prior 736872bdde1af7ad5ed7cdd42ebae9e24a7ca1ba09bc63a2f19abd4f7b9833f1. Existing ENABLE_RUST_KERNEL default ON, RUST_KERNEL_ENABLED cpu.c macro and lib.rs module select the Rust path. Retained selected.o defines save_fp_regs/imports Rust; actual_save.o defines Rust; fallback.o has no Rust import. Full production consumer/link remains unproved.

boundary_analysis.invariant: Owned preallocated state, allocation and publication order
boundary_analysis.evidence: Valid aligned live Thread is an unsafe caller precondition, as in existing C. Raw field accesses make no aliasing Rust references. Availability0 returns without touching thread or state. Nonzero availability and positive size allocate only for null fp_regs. Existing state is neither reallocated nor cleared. Successful new state is zeroed across the whole rounded extent before fp_regs publication, then XSAVE. ENOMEM reports original error, preserves null pointer and returns -12 before any XSAVE. No recoverable post-publication error/leak path exists.

boundary_analysis.invariant: Page arithmetic, geometry and bridge ABI
boundary_analysis.evidence: Positive i32 size converts to usize on x86_64; pages<=524288 and rounded bytes<=2147483648, so addition/product/page-count cast cannot overflow. Existing allocator signature/flags match int,int,unsigned-long,int,int,unsigned-long,char*,int and pointer return; uses pages,0,2,-1,0,ULONG_MAX,diagnostic CPU_FILE,line. Allocator page alignment exceeds required64. A preallocated buffer must cover the boot-stable CPUID standard extent. No new validator is claimed.

boundary_analysis.invariant: XSAVE asm register, memory and ordering contract
boundary_analysis.evidence: asm uses state in(reg), low32 in eax, high32 in edx and xsave [state]; EAX/EDX cannot overlap independent state input. XSAVE leaves these GPR inputs and arithmetic flags intact. nostack and preserves_flags apply to the instruction; no nomem/readonly/pure suppresses its memory writes or side effects. Compiler therefore sees read/write memory side effects and orders publication/zeroing before XSAVE. Actual pinned Rust1.92 object loads Thread fp_regs at0x12b0, calls memset before store, splits RCX into EDX:EAX at a5/ac and executes single XSAVE at ae. Allocation failure branches to error print/return and bypasses XSAVE. Same non-REX.W XSAVE instruction form as preserved C.

Retained actual save object uses GPR operations and allocator/memset/kprintf calls; it contains no XMM/YMM/ZMM/x87/XRSTOR instructions and exactly one XSAVE. Flags match production no-SIMD recipe. Inherited rustc1.92 disabled-sse2 host ABI warning retained; this ABI uses only pointers and integer scalars. Final linked transitive allocator/memset/kprintf no-FP/SIMD closure must still be checked. Kernel use of FP/SIMD in these callees would corrupt unsaved live state.

boundary_analysis.invariant: Real Thread ABI and caller exclusion
boundary_analysis.evidence: Rust uses actual repr(C) Thread from abi.rs; fixture asserts size5568/alignment64/fp_regs4784 and object accesses offset4784. C seam fixture uses a stand-in, so production-header C DWARF/ABI binding remains required. Existing sched_schedule_fp_admit disables IRQ before reading current and saving, and panics on nonzero save before runqueue preparation. New retained subprocess links actual admission+save bodies and observes irq-save/cpu-local/allocate/allocation-error/panic only. Other existing clone/idle-init caller contracts and behavior are preserved, not newly certified.

boundary_analysis.invariant: Controlled oracle is not hardware acceptance
boundary_analysis.evidence: 480 vectors compare preserved original C against actual Rust save body with XSAVE leaf replaced by controlled fixture. Full-page zeroing, preallocated bytes/tails, guards, unchanged neighboring Thread bytes, allocation ABI, ENOMEM order and full64bit masks are checked. Nonzero availability with nonpositive size and absent state reaches seam only: invalid hardware geometry, never a valid native positive. Arbitrary masks and tiny sizes are seam vectors, not claims of CPUID-supported XSAVE configurations. No null XSAVE or hardware XSAVE ran.

Only copy harness change peels preserved save fallback before its unchanged full pre-copy-source SHA256 assertion. It does not alter the copy oracle, expectations or implementation. Retained copy-regression-2 passes64 parity+8invalid configurations+2null pointers. This verifies regression seam/object behavior, not hardware or production proof.

boundary_analysis.invariant: Language boundary and frozen current image
boundary_analysis.evidence: New implementation is Rust plus reviewed XSAVE assembly. C addition is minimal ABI/config forwarding; original C fallback and accepted restore/release/default paths remain preserved. Optional debug allocation/TID dkprintf traces are omitted; failure kprintf remains. Candidate remains private; current frozen combined first-two-port build/image and separate post-switch-exit candidate were not modified.
